title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-12-01
taper: 3 great sources of this music were provided by ANON to make this version, 2 were used Almost Certainly Recorded by Peter Abrams

ai_review.summary: Remastered 12/1/66 show with hiss largely gone (though a bit thin on high‑end) and an eclectic early‑Dead set highlighted by Cream Puff War and One Kind Favor.
ai_review.review: The new source dramatically reduces the tape hiss that plagued earlier releases, delivering a clear enough picture of this 1966 performance even if some sparkle in the highs is missing. The show itself is a lively snapshot of the band’s formative era – heavy on organ, surf‑rock riffs and bluesy jams with Cream Puff War standing out, while the overall playing feels enthusiastic but still raw.

ai_rating.rationale: Two detailed reviews praise the remaster’s clarity and the show’s energy despite minor high‑frequency loss; limited sample size keeps confidence at medium.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss largely removed in the new remaster, but the high end is attenuated; overall sound is clear enough for a 1966 tape source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑Dead set mixes 60's surf‑rock, bluesy jams and folk covers; eclectic and a bit uneven but captures the band's exploratory spirit.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Lead guitar featured prominently; reviewers note his strong presence throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work mentioned as solid, providing the low‑end foundation for the early jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm/lead attempts are noted (“hitting with Minglewood but not quite there”).
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ/keyboard heavy; reviewers describe a “heavy on the keys” texture in the first set.
